data.narrative:
Proteus Space is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by David Kervin (20+ years in US military government contracting) and Andrew Shapiro (20 years at NASA JPL, managed technology formulation including 3D-printed components for Mars Perseverance). The company has raised $14.4M to date. The broader Space & Aerospace sector comprises 6 public comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable method given data constraints. Using $17M as a proxy for total capital deployed and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $34M. This reflects the standard step-up between early and growth-stage rounds in the sector. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, only 2 are adjacent-stage and none meet similarity thresholds; applying an all-sector median would lack specificity. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiple (sector median 27.4x across 5 tickers) cannot proceed without target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $29M–$39M, centered on $34M. Primary uncertainty stems from limited comparable data at this stage and tier; the single-method basis also constrains confidence. Revenue trajectory and contract wins remain critical value drivers not yet quantifiable in this dataset.
